_what: Trail-set RE-SELECTION for twelve east-extension stops. Earlier passes took the trail names already on each card and found links for them; nobody asked whether they were the right trails, or whether there were enough of them for the length of the stay. This patch asks what each box SHOULD hold — roughly one good walk per night, capped at six — and supplies what was missing.
_rules: Every trail carries distance, time, difficulty and reviews, or says which of those could not be sourced. Every URL was copied from a search result, never assembled from a name. `dogs` is set only from the managing authority's own words, quoted in `dogs_source_quote`; where the authority publishes nothing the field is absent, because 'we did not check' must never read as 'dogs are welcome'.

trails.name: Lost Creek Falls Trail
trails.note: Bayfield County Forestry has boardwalked a good share of the 1.5 mi in to the falls; you can walk behind the 8 ft plunge, which is unusual on this shore. About 20 mi west of Bayfield at Cornucopia — the nearest genuinely good walk to camp that is not on the Apostle Islands shoreline.

other_links.label: Bayfield County — Hiking
other_links.note: The managing authority (Bayfield County Forestry and Parks). Confirms the boardwalk and gives the walk as roughly 3 mi round trip from the Trail Road trailhead.

trails.stats_note: Review count read twice and drifted: 839 on one index, 893 on another. Good enough to order the box, not to quote. Bayfield County publishes no pet rule for this trail, so `dogs` is deliberately absent rather than assumed.

trails.name: Morgan Falls and St Peter's Dome Trail
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets must always be restrained or on a leash while in developed recreation sites.
trails.note: Two destinations on one walk — a 70 ft falls and the bald granite dome, with Lake Superior and the Apostle Islands from the top. AllTrails grades it Easy despite 528 ft of gain; reviewers report wet, root-bound ground for much of it. Marengo, about 45 mi south of Bayfield.

alltrails.name: Morgan Falls and St Peter's Dome Trail

other_links.label: USFS — St. Peters Dome / Morgan Falls
other_links.note: Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest's own page for the site.

trails.stats_note: The slug carries a --2 suffix; a shorter listing at .../morgan-falls-and-st-peters-dome-trail is a different, 1.6 mi route to the falls alone (4.6, 166 reviews). Both URLs were copied from results, not built.

trails.name: Doughboys Nature Trail, Copper Falls State Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: If you are bringing a pet to Copper Falls, please note that pets are not allowed on the Doughboys Nature Trail that goes to Copper and Brownstone Falls. There is no trail to view Copper and Brownstone Falls with your pet. ... Please remember pets cannot be left unattended at any time while in the park, this includes in your vehicle or campsite.
trails.note: The best-reviewed walk within reach of this stop and the one the dog cannot do — and the DNR also forbids leaving her in the truck while you do it, so this is a walk only if someone stays with her. About 55 mi south of Bayfield near Mellen. The dog-legal substitute inside the same park is the Red Granite Falls Trail, linked below.

alltrails.name: North Country Scenic and Doughboy's Loop

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Copper Falls hiking (and the pets notice)
other_links.note: Source of the 1.7 mi official length, the winter partial closure of the rock stairs, and the pet ban.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Red Granite Falls Trail (the pet-legal alternative)
other_links.note: 2.5 mi loop, 196 ft, 0.5-1 hr, 4.6 from 765 reviews. Wide gravel from Loon Lake. The DNR calls it 'the only waterfall trail open to pets' at Copper Falls, and the falls there are unfenced.

trails.stats_note: AllTrails indexes the park's Doughboys loop under a North Country Trail name; the official name and length come from the DNR. Review count drifted between indexes (947 and 1,312) — approximate, and used only to order the box.

trails.name: Hotz Trail and Europe Bay Loop, Newport State Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted in most campgrounds, trails, roads and outlying areas of properties. ... Pets are not allowed in ... Beaches, except designated pet swim areas ... Trails marked as closed to pets.
trails.note: Newport is Wisconsin's only wilderness state park and an International Dark Sky Park; nothing else in the county is this quiet. The card had nothing north of Fish Creek before this. The loop runs the shore of Europe Lake and Lake Michigan — the walking is dog-legal but the beaches it touches are not.

alltrails.name: Hotz Trail and Europe Bay Loop

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Newport State Park hiking
other_links.note: The authority's own trail list. It gives the full Europe Bay trail loop as 7.0 miles, hiking and bike, mostly level on old logging roads — the AllTrails 2.8 mi loop is the short Hotz combination, not the whole thing.

trails.name: Tower Trail, Potawatomi State Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are permitted in most campgrounds, trails, roads and outlying areas of properties.
trails.note: The Sturgeon Bay end of the peninsula, which nothing on the card covered. Oak and cedar down to the Sturgeon Bay shore, rocky and rooty near the water. The observation tower itself has been closed for rebuilding in recent seasons — worth confirming before driving down for it, but the trail is the point.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Ice Age Trail and Tower Trail
other_links.note: The longer version if the short loop is not enough: 6.0 mi, 331 ft, moderate, 2-2.5 hr, 4.6 from 606 reviews.

trails.stats_note: Tower-closure claim not sourced to the DNR here — treat as a thing to check, not a fact. The trail figures are AllTrails'.

trails.name: Pothole Trail - Cedar Ridge Trail, Rockwood Conservation Area
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are welcome, but owners must follow some very important rules ... Keep your dog on a leash that's less than 2 m/6 ft long ... Make sure your dog stays on marked trails.
trails.note: The best-reviewed walk within half an hour of Elora and the obvious replacement for the Quarry, which bars dogs outright. Limestone cliffs, caves and one of the world's largest glacial potholes above the Eramosa River, plus the ruined Harris woollen mill. Same authority as the Gorge, so the same 2 m leash rule applies.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Rockwood Conservation Area browse
other_links.note: Park-level page; four listed trails. Candidate for AREA_BROWSE_ALLTRAILS if a Rockwood day is planned.

trails.stats_note: Review count read at 2,046, 2,207 and 2,248 across indexes on the same day. Approximate; used to order, not to quote.

trails.name: Forks of the Credit Trail
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are welcome at all Ontario Parks, and are permitted on campsites, park roads and most hiking trails, except for a few specific campgrounds and sensitive areas.
trails.season: Kettle Trail and the Cataract Falls viewpoint are at their best in the first half of October; the stop arrives 31 Aug, which is green-leaf, not colour.
trails.note: The far end of the Elora Cataract Trailway that already sits on this card — the Trailway finishes here, at the ruined Cataract power house and the falls on the Credit. About 55 km east of Elora in Caledon; the biggest single walk available from this stop and the only one with real climbing.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Forks of the Credit Provincial Park browse
other_links.note: Seven listed trails; the park page is the AREA_BROWSE candidate.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Cataract Falls via Trans Canada Trail and Kettle Trail Loop
other_links.note: Shorter alternative to the full loop if 977 ft is more than the day wants.

trails.stats_note: Only the en-gb locale returned a www AllTrails URL for this trail; a us-locale copy appeared solely on the plp. subdomain and was not used, because rewriting a host is constructing a URL. Review count varied 1,550 / 1,798 / 1,904 across indexes.

trails.name: Millennium Trail
trails.distance: 29.9 mi point-to-point (49 km corridor end to end per the County)
trails.time: 9.5-10.5 hr end to end — walked or ridden in sections
trails.dogs_source_quote: The trail is popular amongst a wide array of recreational enthusiasts year round including walkers, hikers, joggers, cyclists, ATV riders, dirt bikers (licensed & insured), horseback riders and dog walkers.
trails.cruise_reason: It is a former rail bed and flat enough, but the County permits ATVs and licensed dirt bikes on it outside winter, and users report the surface churned and rutted where they have run. That is the surface risk §4 exists to catch — ride it, but scout the section first rather than trusting the rail-grade.
trails.note: The four trails already on this card are all short Sandbanks dune-and-wood loops; there was no long flat walk or ride anywhere on it. The Millennium runs the old Prince Edward County Railway from Carrying Place to Picton through wetland and farmland, and is the one place in the County you can put in an easy hour or five without a car.

other_links.label: PEC Trails — trail users and permitted uses
other_links.note: The County's trails committee. Source of the permitted-use list, including the ATV and dirt-bike permission.

other_links.label: Ontario Trails Council — Millennium Trail, Prince Edward County
other_links.note: Gives the corridor as 49 km, Carrying Place to Picton.

trails.stats_note: The AllTrails listing treats the whole corridor as one 29.9 mi route, which is why its time is a full day; nobody walks it that way. No star rating was returned in any result read for this listing — only the 98-review count from the page title — so none is recorded. The trail's standing comes from the County, not from AllTrails.

trails.name: Sandstone Island Trail, Charleston Lake Provincial Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are welcome at all Ontario Parks, and are permitted on campsites, park roads and most hiking trails, except for a few specific campgrounds and sensitive areas.
trails.note: All three trails already on this card are Thousand Islands National Park sites on the river. This is the granite-and-lake side of the same country, 30 km north near Lansdowne: Canadian Shield outcrops, First Nations rock shelters used for two thousand years, pioneer foundations and a lookout over Charleston Lake. Ontario Parks' 2 m leash applies and the dog stays off the beach.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Charleston Lake Provincial Park browse
other_links.note: Four listed trails; Sandstone Island is the most popular of them.

other_links.label: Ontario Trails Council — Sandstone Island Trail
other_links.note: Confirms the rock shelters and the Charleston Lake lookout.

trails.name: Foley Mountain Loop Trail (Spy Rock), Foley Mountain Conservation Area
trails.dogs_source_quote: Foley Mountain offers a quiet sandy beach on the shores of Upper Rideau Lake ... Dogs are not allowed.
trails.note: Four of the five trails already on this card are Murphys Point or the Rideau Trail through it — one park, over and over. Foley Mountain is the other landscape of this country: a granite ridge above Upper Rideau Lake at Westport with the Spy Rock lookout, roughly 40 km from Perth. Dirt and gravel underfoot with rock outcrops, not technical.

other_links.label: Rideau Valley Conservation Authority — Foley Mountain
other_links.note: The managing authority. 10 km of trails, open year round but unmaintained in winter. The only pet prohibition it publishes for the property is the beach.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Foley Mountain Conservation Area browse

trails.stats_note: Only the en-gb locale returned a www URL for this trail. The RVCA states a dog ban for its beaches and asks on its Foley Mountain page for dogs to be leashed on conservation-area trails; it publishes no trail ban, so `dogs: true` is recorded with the beach carved out. Separately, and worth knowing at this stop: the RVCA does bar dogs entirely from the Perth Wildlife Reserve.
trails.needs: star rating is from AllTrails' area page rather than the trail title; count read at 657, 675 and 686 on the same day

trails.name: Mt. Van Hoevenberg
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the Eastern Zone of the High Peaks Wilderness and at trailheads, campsites and above 4,000 feet everywhere else.
trails.season: Late September is the front edge of Adirondack colour; the open summit ledges here look straight at Marcy, Colden and the MacIntyres, so this is the view walk of the stop.
trails.note: The card had Mount Jo, Owl's Head and Cascade-Porter — two very short ones and one Hard 4,000-footer, with nothing moderate in between. This is the gap-filler: a real summit with a real view for half a day's work, on a purpose-built graded trail rather than an Adirondack root ladder. Dog legal but must be leashed — this is inside the Eastern High Peaks zone, where rangers write about ten off-leash tickets a year.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Mt. Van Hoevenberg East Trail
other_links.note: The newer, better-liked way up, from the Olympic Sports Complex side: 3.7 mi out-and-back, 974 ft, 4.8 from 3,811 reviews — the highest-rated walk anywhere near Lake Placid. No estimated time or difficulty grade was returned for it in any result read, which is the only reason the older trail carries the entry.

trails.needs: star rating — no result read returned one for this listing, only the 2,388-review count from the page title

trails.name: Baker Mountain Loop Trail
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be leashed at all times in the Eastern Zone of the High Peaks Wilderness and at trailheads, campsites and above 4,000 feet everywhere else.
trails.note: Half an hour's drive for Saranac Lake's steepest half hour on foot — 879 ft in under a mile up, then lookouts over Saranac Lake, Lake Flower and the whole High Peaks skyline. Part of the Saranac 6er. It is in the McKenzie Mountain Wilderness, outside the Eastern High Peaks zone, so the DEC leash rule binds at the trailhead rather than the whole way; leash her anyway on something this busy.

other_links.label: Saranac Lake — Baker Mountain
other_links.note: Local visitor bureau: 1.6 mi round trip, 884 ft of gain, summit 2,452 ft. Slightly shorter than the AllTrails loop, which adds the Moody Pond return.

trails.stats_note: A separate AllTrails listing simply named 'Baker Mountain' shows a review count of 2,454 — identical to the mountain's height in feet, which is exactly the coincidence §2 says to distrust. The loop listing was used instead. No star rating was returned for either.

trails.name: Coaticook Gorge Park Loop (Parc de la Gorge de Coaticook)
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are also allowed inside the park, but must be kept on a leash at all times.
trails.season: First half of October is peak colour in the Townships and the gorge is a hardwood canyon — this is the week for it.
trails.note: This card was in trouble: three of its four trails are inside Parc national du Mont-Orford, where Sépaq's coloured map bans dogs from the whole massif network. Coaticook is the first entry on it the dog can actually walk. A 50 m deep canyon on the Coaticook River crossed by the longest pedestrian suspension bridge in North America, plus an observation tower, a dam and a cave. About 55 km east of the stop.

other_links.label: Parc de la Gorge de Coaticook — hiking trails
other_links.note: The managing authority. 19 km of marked trail across three areas; source of the dog rule and of the admission-fee structure.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Coaticook Gorge
other_links.note: A second, shorter listing for the same park under a different name, 287 reviews — the canyon-only walk rather than the full loop.

trails.needs: star rating — none returned in any result read

trails.name: Mount Pinnacle Trail, Parc Harold F. Baldwin (Mont Pinacle)
trails.dogs_source_quote: Oui, les chiens sont permis tant qu'ils sont tenus en laisse tout au long de la randonnee. Nous vous demandons de ramasser les besoins du chien et les jeter a la poubelle.
trails.season: Maple forest the whole way up; 5-11 Oct is the week it is worth driving for.
trails.note: The second dog-legal walk this stop needed, and the best-reviewed trail in the whole Coaticook area — an isolated Appalachian hill standing 194 m above Lac Lyster, with the lake and Little Lake Baldwin from the top at 665 m. Paid day access, bookable online. Peregrine falcons and owls; it is also a climbing crag, so expect ropes at the base.

other_links.label: Parc Harold F. Baldwin — FAQ (the dog rule)
other_links.note: The managing authority answers the dog question directly. Its own site gives the park as roughly 63 ha with 6 trails, 7 km round trip in total.

other_links.label: Cantons-de-l'Est — Mont Pinacle
other_links.note: Regional tourism board; gives the summit as 665 m and a 3 km climb, and also lists the trail as 'Chien admis en laisse'.

trails.stats_note: Considered separately and rejected: Round Top at the Parc d'environnement naturel de Sutton, the other famous Townships summit. PENS' own rules read 'PAS DE CHIEN dans la Reserve naturelle des Montagnes-Vertes ... interdits dans tous les sentiers indiques en rouge sur notre carte', and whether the Round Top summit trail is one of the red ones could not be settled from here. On a card that already carries three dog-banned Mont-Orford trails, a fourth maybe was not worth adding. Worth a phone call to PENS if Sutton is wanted.
trails.needs: count read at 2,211, 2,247, 2,289, 2,368 and 2,371 across indexes on the same day — ordering figure only

trails.name: Woods Loop Trail, Beech Hill Preserve
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs are NOT permitted at Fernalds Neck, Rockport Shore, or Hodson Preserves.
trails.season: Open blueberry barrens rather than canopy, so it reads well even once the leaves are down — which by 22-27 Oct they largely are on the midcoast.
trails.note: Every trail on this card was a Camden Hills State Park summit climb, three of them on the same ridge. Beech Hill is the other kind of day: an easy walk up organic blueberry barrens in Rockport to Beech Nut, the sod-roofed stone hut built in 1914, with Penobscot Bay, the Camden Hills and the St George peninsula laid out around it. The land trust names the three preserves where dogs are barred and this is not one of them; its maps page adds 'If not posted, dogs must be on leash.'

other_links.label: Coastal Mountains Land Trust — Beech Hill Preserve
other_links.note: The managing authority. Two ways up: Summit Trail 0.6 mi one-way, easy, from Beech Hill Road, which is the wheelchair-accessible one; Woods Loop 0.9 mi one-way, easy, from Rockville Street.

other_links.label: Coastal Mountains Land Trust — Preserve Use Guidelines
other_links.note: Source of the dog rule. Worth reading before picking any other preserve near Camden: Fernalds Neck, on Megunticook Lake and otherwise an obvious choice for this stop, is one of the three that bar dogs.

trails.name: Rockland Breakwater Trail
trails.season: Open granite with no shelter at all — a fine late-October walk on a calm day and a bad one in wind or rain, when the blocks are slick and uneven.
trails.note: The one flat, sea-level walk within reach of this stop: 4,300 ft of granite block straight out into Rockland Harbor to the 1902 breakwater light, with the windjammer fleet going past. Nineteen feet of elevation gain against four ridge climbs on the rest of the card.

other_links.label: TravelMaine — Rockland Breakwater Trail
other_links.note: Gives the pier as 7/8 mile and lists pets as permitted — but this is a tourism directory, not the owner, so no `dogs` value is recorded here.

trails.stats_note: No managing-authority pet rule was found for the breakwater, which is federal granite with the light maintained by a friends group and the shore end in city hands, so `dogs` is deliberately absent. Uneven, gapped blocks are a real consideration for a dog regardless of the rule. No star rating was returned for the listing.

trails.name: Bash Bish Falls from Taconic State Park
trails.dogs_source_quote: Pets are to be supervised at all times and must be crated or on a leash not more than 6-feet in length. ... Pets are not permitted in playgrounds, buildings, golf courses, boardwalks, pools and spray-grounds or guarded swim areas/beaches.
trails.note: The tallest waterfall in Massachusetts, and the obvious hole in a card that otherwise climbed Greylock twice. Approach it from the New York side, from Taconic State Park at Copake Falls: it is the gentler walk, the better-reviewed one, and the one that has stayed open. DCR has closed the Massachusetts trail from Falls Road repeatedly for erosion and drainage work — a full closure through 12 Jun 2025, and further closures on selected days since. Not a seasonal closure and not predictable two years out, so check DCR before driving to the Mount Washington lot rather than assuming either way. Swimming is prohibited on both sides.

alltrails.name: Bash Bish Falls from Taconic State Park

other_links.label: AllTrails — Bash Bish Falls Trail (the Massachusetts approach)
other_links.note: The short, steep way down from the Falls Road lot in Mount Washington: 538 ft of gain, 1,460 reviews. This is the side subject to the DCR closures.

other_links.label: iBerkshires — Access to Bash Bish Falls Remains Closed for Trail Work
other_links.note: The 2025 closure in DCR's own words as reported locally: 21 Apr to 12 Jun 2025, Mount Washington side only, with the falls still reachable from Taconic State Park in New York.

trails.stats_note: `dogs` is sourced to New York State Parks because the recommended walk starts and mostly runs on their ground. Massachusetts DCR's own pet page could not be read — mass.gov answers 403 to every automated fetch from here — so the Massachusetts side is NOT covered by this verdict and would need checking separately.

trails.name: Cobble Hill Loop, Tyringham Cobble
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs must be kept on leash at all times.
trails.season: By 27-31 Oct the Berkshire canopy has usually gone over — Berkshire colour peaks nearer 5-15 Oct — which suits this one: the point of the Cobble is the open meadow and the view down the Tyringham valley, and that only improves once the leaves are off.
trails.note: A short, steep quartzite knob with the Appalachian Trail over the top and Rabbit Rock on the way down, in the prettiest valley in the southern Berkshires. Same owner as Monument Mountain, which is already on this card, so the rules and the parking work the same way. The Trustees call it 'moderate hiking, strenuous in places' — the summit pitch is the strenuous part.

other_links.label: The Trustees — Tyringham Cobble
other_links.note: The managing authority. '2-mile loop trail. Moderate hiking, strenuous in places.' Source of the dog rule.

other_links.label: The Trustees — Dog Friendly Hiking Trails
other_links.note: The Trustees' master list of which reservations allow dogs on leash, which allow off-leash, and which bar them. Worth consulting before adding any other Trustees property to this leg.

trails.name: Steep Rock Centennial-Yellow Circle Loop, Steep Rock Preserve
trails.dogs_source_quote: Steep Rock Association's pet policy is in compliance with CT Law requiring pet owners to keep their dogs 'under control' at all times on public property. Steep Rock Association has defined 'under control' as meaning the dog is tethered to a leash.
trails.season: 31 Oct - 5 Nov is past leaf-peak in the Litchfield hills, but the first mile is a river-level former rail bed, which holds colour later than the ridges and walks well in the wet.
trails.note: The four trails on this card are all state-park properties and three of them are short. Steep Rock is the region's best-loved walk and the only large private preserve on the leg — 998 acres and about 20 miles of trail on a bend of the Shepaug River, with the tunnel and the old Shepaug Valley Railroad grade. The loop begins flat on the rail bed for roughly a mile, then climbs; horses are barred above that point, which is a fair marker of where it stiffens.

other_links.label: Steep Rock Association — Pets in Our Preserves
other_links.note: The managing authority's dog policy. Waste bins at most trailheads.

other_links.label: Steep Rock Association — Steep Rock Preserve
other_links.note: 998 acres, trails along the river banks and up into the hillsides above.

other_links.label: Connecticut Trail Finder — Steep Rock Preserve
other_links.note: Names the other loops if the day wants something shorter — the Clamshell Loop for the Shepaug valley view, or the 776 ft Steep Rock summit.

trails.stats_note: Steep Rock Association permits regulated hunting on some of its land and the stop falls inside Connecticut's autumn deer season. Nothing was found either way for this preserve specifically; check the Association's site for season notices before walking here on a weekday in early November.

trails.name: Awosting Falls Carriage Road, Minnewaska State Park Preserve
trails.dogs_source_quote: Dogs only, must be on a leash not more than 6 feet. Not allowed in buildings, camping, picnic or bathing areas or on walkways. Pets are NOT permitted at beaches or on the cross-country ski trails when they are groomed and open for cross-country skiing only.
trails.season: 5-11 Nov is past colour on the Shawangunk ridge, but this is a waterfall and a cliff-edge carriage road rather than a leaf walk, and November flow is usually better than October's.
trails.note: Everything on this card sat on the river — the Roosevelt and Vanderbilt estates, the Walkway, Storm King. Nothing went up onto the Shawangunks, which is the landscape people come to the Hudson Valley for. This is the gentlest way onto it: crushed-stone carriage road with no scrambling, past the 60 ft Awosting Falls and around Lake Minnewaska on the clifftop. Rideable as well as walkable, and 87% of reviewers call it easy despite the Moderate grade.

other_links.label: New York State Parks — Minnewaska State Park Preserve
other_links.note: The managing authority: 35 miles of carriage road and 50 miles of footpath, and the pet rule quoted above. Note the preserve's gates close early in winter and the lot fills at weekends.

other_links.label: AllTrails — Awosting Falls Connection Trail to Awosting Falls
other_links.note: The short version — roughly a mile to the falls and back from the lower lot, if 5.5 mi is more than the day wants.

trails.stats_note: Count read at 585 and 611 on the same day; the 4.6 star figure came with the 585 reading. Ordering figure only.
